argument: one repair after each recorded answer; upward rounding on a binary grid; normalized stored coordinate intervals; a refinement-rarity lemma P=O(q/k); finite enclosing intervals and a bounded recursive phase
formalization: Related earlier integer-colour construction; this continuous presentation is not formally verified.
exposition: Section 3 presents the updated controller, one repair after an answer, records with fully propagated bounds, and explicit normalization. Section 4 keeps the volume identity and geometric example, the remaining-order proof, and the new rarity argument. Section 5 keeps rounding, the useful central-density bound, one-arc repair, and the two-move progress argument. Section 6 explains the finite update and monotone enclosure. Section 7 retains the finite horizon and clocked parameter selection. Geometry, certificate calibration, refinement estimates, consistency details and arithmetic inventories are in appendices. The main text ends on page 21. The abstract, disclosure and all figures except the obsolete anchor tree are unchanged. Section 1 now states and cites the information-theoretic lower bound. Section 2 adds Fredman's comparison bound and its relation to Kahn and Kim's polynomial-time algorithm.

source_material: The complete latest assistant message in Simplify Paper Arguments, retrieved through the connected chat reader: 15,850 characters, not truncated. It proposes simplifications and proof placement against d0da5c2. The linked eleven-page PDF and source archive were not downloaded. The proposal was implemented in the existing manuscript and independently reviewed; exact diagnostics for rounding, one-arc repair and rarity were added or revised.
implementation_change: The answer-selection loop refines only queried labels after a failed certificate, at most twice, using the middle half directly. After recording the answer, one complete path batch in path order or one degree repair restores the strict bounds. Refine passes its reason to ChooseAnchor, which uses central certification only for structural repairs. Normalize propagates all bounds in two topological passes. RoundUp replaces minimum-depth anchor search. The rarity bound gives P=O(Q(n)/k+n) including an unfinished call; stored precision is O(n log^2 n).
editorial_revision: Move the logarithm notation and n >= 2 convention to a footnote on the first sentence of the Introduction. No other manuscript changes.
